subject: Integration discovery: SDK/auth + observability checkpoints for CobaltAI
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Alex Grant <alex@cobaltai.com>, Diana Lopez <diana.lopez@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Apr 2026 13:02:00 -0700
Subject: Integration discovery: SDK/auth + observability checkpoints for CobaltAI

Alex / Diana — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment before the technical deep-dive.

Highlights from today's discovery:
- Goal: replace existing on-prem text-ranking pipeline with Redwood-hosted inference for reranking + embeddings. Primary constraints are P99 latency <120ms for rerank calls, and EU data residency.
- Scope: initial pilot will include SDK integration for embedding/rerank clients, service-to-service auth (short-lived keys), and observability hooks for tracing across your API gateway.

Architectural checkpoints we agreed to validate in the next session:
1) SDK & Auth
   - Use Redwood Node SDK (v0.9.x) — we can provide a small code snippet for quickstart.
   - Service-to-service auth: short-lived API keys via your internal vault (we recommend rotating 1h keys) or mTLS if you prefer.
2) Routing & Model variants
   - Primary route: reranker (low-latency variant), fallback route: high-throughput quantized model for bulk ops.
   - We will show how to pin model versions and configure automatic fallback in the Console.
3) Structured output / tool-calling
   - We will validate the structured output schema for the reranker (JSON score + explanation field) and an optional tool-call flow for enrichment.
4) Embeddings / Rerankers
   - Embeddings stored in your vector DB (we saw you use Vespa today) — Redwood will produce stable vector dims and metadata fields (source_id, chunk_idx).
5) Observability hooks (must-haves)
   - Trace propagation: we recommend passing X-Redwood-Trace and echoing it in logs.
   - Per-request headers: X-Redwood-Latency (server, queue, model) for latency breakdowns.
   - Logging fields: request_id, model_version, route, seq_len, batch_size; include user_id in PCI-free hashed form.
   - Dashboard: we will provide a pre-built dashboard (tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, cache hit rate, error rate) and a set of alert thresholds.

Requested items from your side before the tech call:
- Temporary test account with a sandbox API key scoped to embeddings+generation (no PII).
- A copy of the security questionnaire (you can attach or paste answers).
- Example request/response from your current reranker for endpoint parity checks.

Proposed next steps:
- Tech deep-dive with Marissa (engineer) and Lauren (solutions) — 60-minute session. Suggested: Wed Apr 14 09:00-10:00 CEST.
- I'll share a short integration checklist and a sample config file prior to the call.

Attachments: sample-redwood-config.yaml (YAML) — includes SDK snippet and header examples.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Karthik
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.com
+1 415-555-0199

Subject: Re: Integration discovery: SDK/auth + observability checkpoints for CobaltAI

Karthik — thanks for the clear summary. Couple quick clarifications before the deep-dive: 

1) Data residency: EU-first. We'll need the pilot to run in the Frankfurt region. Any limitation on model variants in that region?
2) Auth: we prefer short-lived keys pulled from our Vault; can your SDK pick up creds from environment variables / AWS Secrets Manager?
3) Observability: good to see the X-Redwood-Latency header — can you confirm the three breakdown components you populate (queue, compute, model)? Also we want the trace id to appear in our gateway logs as `cobalt_trace_id` — are you ok with mirroring the incoming request id header if present?

Attached is our completed security questionnaire (redacted) and a small reranker sample output.

Also, small ask on SLOs: for the reranker path (single document rerank) we target p95 < 70ms in steady-state — can you point to the closest performance profile you have?

Happy to take the Wed slot you suggested; the team confirms Wed Apr 14 at 09:00 CEST.

Best,
Alex Grant
Head of Infrastructure | CobaltAI
alex@cobaltai.com
+44 20 7946 0857

--

Looping in a few engineer notes before the Wed call — internal-only.

Marissa notes:
- We should pre-generate a small set of model profiles for Frankfurt: low-latency reranker (v2-rls), quantized throughput (q4_0). I can run benchmarks on a 1-GPU seed to validate p95 numbers; will report back by EOD Tue (Apr 13).
- SDK auth: Node SDK already supports env var creds and AWS Secrets Manager via a small wrapper. I'll add code snippets to the Drive doc.
- Observability: implement middleware that maps incoming `cobalt_request_id` -> X-Redwood-Trace and emits both to logs. Also add X-Redwood-Latency with three subfields: queue_ms|compute_ms|model_ms. Example header: X-Redwood-Latency: 5|20|40

Action items for Wed call:
1) Marissa: bring perf numbers for the two model profiles (p50/p95/p99) in Frankfurt.
2) Lauren: bring rollout plan for canary -> prod (how to pin model and fallback).
3) Karthik: share the sample config and the Drive link with CobaltAI.

I'll prep a short runbook snippet for the latency header mapping and push it to Drive before the call.

—Marissa
